driver: Several pools of returnable containers circulate between a plant and many holders, and each pool's shortfall in its worst forward week decides whether it is bought, hired or left alone; no record holds what the holders have, how many containers are still alive, or what the plant's store will hold. The field team's counts at the holders see the full containers on the day an order is taken and never the emptied ones waiting to be collected, so what a holder has must be rebuilt from its own deliveries before any relation to its throughput is fitted; the store takes each item a whole production run at a time, so its stock follows the runs and the number of items on sale, which the forward plan changes; and the register never loses a container, so the yearly loss has to be estimated from how the share of each purchase lot still found on site falls with the lot's age. The counts fitted as they stand, days of cover and the register as the fleet pass every check the record allows and understate every pool.
driver_concrete: Wrenfold reads each pool's largest weekly shortfall in the 2027 summer season against two lines in its fleet standard (none: hold; under the maker's minimum order run: hire for the season; the minimum order run or more: buy). The reps count a line's full containers on the account's order day, four to six days after the dray on a weekly round, so the counts miss the empties: fitted as they stand they give a line 0.09 to 0.33 containers per container sold a week where the line holds 0.78 to 1.04, and the five pools' summer rise is 5,741 containers where the counts as they stand give 3,604; the 2027 brew plan's longer runs and wider range put 10,417 full containers in the store at its fullest where 2026's weeks of cover give 6,414; and the register holds 114,676 containers where about 48,550 are alive, the trade losing 5,103 a year (2.9 to 13.0 per cent of each pool), read from the share of each purchase lot the count of 30 November 2026 found on site. Figures from generator/core.py at the draw; the cut pack's replace them.
stump: A careful but hurried analyst fits what a line holds on the cellar counts as they stand (the 50 litre shortfall then falls under the maker's minimum run where it clears it), carries 2026's store cover in weeks to 2027's deliveries (the 20 litre pool then has kegs to spare where it is hundreds short under the summer range's 200-keg runs), and takes the fleet at the count forward with no loss, because the register shows none (the firkins' shortfall then falls under the maker's minimum run where it clears it).
deep_chain: (1) each cellar count turned into what the line holds: the full containers counted and the containers the line has sold since the dray last called, from the day of its last docket and its weekly sales; (2) what a line holds as a fixed number and a number per container sold a week by delivery interval, by pool, checked on the counts' own fall with the containers sold since the delivery; (3) each pool's deliveries week by week through the 2027 season at normal weather and across the ten summers on record, the estate's lines added from their listing dates; (4) the rise in the trade's stock from the count to each season week, the estate's cellars line by line; (5) the share of each purchase lot the count found on site against the lot's age, fitted for the yearly rate of leaving and the share of the fleet on site, by pool, and the fleet alive; (6) the store's stock as its cover beside half a racking run per beer on sale, rebuilt under the 2027 plan's runs, range and dates; (7) each pool's weekly shortfall, its largest in the season in the planning case and in the hot case, and the cover against nil and the maker's minimum run
judgment: a count that sees part of what a holder has, rebuilt from the holder's own delivery cycle; a store stock set by run size and range under a forward plan that changes both; a loss no record holds, estimated from the age structure of what a count finds against a register that never writes off
